Rules
prompt_parts.content:
Rules:
- Translate the block as a coherent passage, not as isolated source lines.
- Do not manually insert @h or speaker names. The tool will wrap lines and create game windows automatically.
- Preserve character voice, narrative flow, and important pauses.
- ASCII apostrophes and contractions are allowed. Do not use curly quotes, em dashes, en dashes, or ellipsis characters.
- The English may be longer or shorter than the Japanese if that improves quality.

prompt_parts.label: Global Style
prompt_parts.content:
Global style:
# Megami Translation Style

Translate into natural English visual-novel prose while preserving the source's pacing and character voice.

Core rules:
- Keep Celica's narration in first person.
- Preserve page rhythm; do not merge or split lines during the pilot.
- Use glossary spellings for names, places, menus, and recurring terms.
- Keep English CP932-safe. Prefer ASCII punctuation.
- Use `...` instead of ellipsis characters and straight quotes instead of curly quotes.
- In the default vanilla text profile, never use apostrophes or contractions.
- In the apostrophe-patched text profile, ASCII apostrophes are allowed.
- Never use em dashes, en dashes, curly quotes, or mojibake punctuation.
- Keep each rendered textbox line at or below 50 visible characters.
- The 50-character limit is a hard technical limit. Shorter and plainer is better than overflowing.
- Speaker pages have one speaker line plus up to 3 dialogue lines.
- Narration pages have up to 4 lines.
- Do not translate script labels unless they are proven visible.
- Translate UI/menu text separately from prose.

Model output rules:
- Return JSON only.
- Return translations keyed by `line_id`.
- Do not invent, remove, or rename line IDs.
- Do not translate speaker names creatively; use glossary names.
- Do not include Japanese in English fields unless a term is intentionally left untranslated.
- If a literal translation is too long, compress it while preserving meaning and tone.

suggestion.en: The god I defeated was a being called an evil god, hostile to the gods who rule this world now. But it was still a god, and because I defeated it and took its power, other gods and their followers called me "God Slayer" and feared me, trying to erase my existence. Over the following decades, since I had obtained a goddess's body and stopped aging, I spent my days fighting and fleeing from most of the world. Eventually, I formed an alliance with the sole god of the great nation of Levia, the "Water Maiden," who belongs to no faction, and gained a temporary haven... For over ten years after that, within Levia, where the Water Maiden is the state religion, attempts on my life by other gods and their followers grew less frequent. But if my true identity were to become known in this town that does not belong to Levia, all its residents would become my enemies, and I would be hunted until I could flee back to Levia. The room is furnished with a lockable chest for belongings, suggesting it is intended for long-term stays.
